_meta.purpose: Classification rules for an LLM agent assigning financial statement row names to canonical sections. Each section includes: description (the WHY), keywords (pattern triggers), examples (real row names from FMP/yfinance/SEC/OpenBB), disambiguation (tricky cases explained), negative_examples (rows that look similar but belong elsewhere), and international_variants (non-US terminology).

Revenue.description: All income generated from the company's PRIMARY operating activities — the top line before any deductions. Includes product sales, service fees, subscriptions, licensing, royalties (when primary business), and rental income (when primary business, e.g. REITs). The test: would this line disappear if the company stopped its core operations? If yes → Revenue. If it would persist as a side activity → Non-Operating Items.
disambiguation: OTHER OPERATING INCOME vs REVENUE: If the label says 'Other Operating Income' and the company's primary business generates it, classify as Revenue. E.g. for a bank 'Other Operating Income' may include fees — Revenue. For a manufacturer, 'Other Operating Income' from subletting a factory floor may be Revenue or Non-Operating depending on materiality.
GAIN ON SALE OF ASSETS: NEVER classify as Revenue. Always Non-Operating Items even if labeled 'Other Income'.
INTEREST INCOME for NON-BANKS: Goes to Non-Operating Items (Investing category). For banks it is Revenue.
NET INTEREST INCOME for BANKS: This IS the revenue equivalent for banks — classify as Revenue.
ROYALTIES: Primary business (publishers, miners) → Revenue. Incidental royalties for a manufacturer → Non-Operating Items.
TENANT REIMBURSEMENTS (REITs): Often shown as a separate line adjacent to rental income — classify as Revenue for REITs.
INTERSEGMENT REVENUE / INTERCOMPANY REVENUE: Usually eliminated in consolidation but if shown, classify as Revenue.
negative_examples: Interest Income (for non-banks — goes to Non-Operating Items)
Gain on Sale of Fixed Assets (Non-Operating)
international_variants: Jingyingshouru / 营业收入 (Chinese PRC GAAP)

Cost of Revenue.description: Direct costs incurred to produce or deliver the goods and services that generate Revenue. The COGS concept. Includes raw materials, direct labor, manufacturing overhead, and D&A on production assets. For software/tech companies: hosting costs, CDN, customer support staff, and amortization of capitalized software. The KEY test: does this cost exist ONLY because a unit of product/service was delivered? If yes → Cost of Revenue.
keywords: cost of goods and services sold
disambiguation: D&A IN COGS vs OPEX: Depreciation on PRODUCTION equipment (factory machinery, data center servers for cloud delivery) belongs in Cost of Revenue. Depreciation on OFFICE equipment or corporate assets belongs in Operating Expenses. If the row is just 'Depreciation and Amortization' without further context, use Operating Expenses.

PROVISION FOR CREDIT LOSSES (BANKS): This is effectively the bank's 'cost of revenue' — classify as Cost of Revenue for banks. It represents the expected credit loss expense tied to generating loan interest income.

FULFILLMENT COSTS (e-commerce like Amazon): These are NOT in COGS but are separate OpEx for most retailers. However Amazon explicitly calls them out separately — classify as Cost of Revenue if labeled 'Fulfillment Costs' or 'Fulfillment Expense'.
TECHNOLOGY AND CONTENT (Amazon/Netflix): Classify as Cost of Revenue when labeled as such. It represents platform delivery costs.
INSURANCE CLAIMS: 'Net Insurance Claims Incurred', 'Policyholder Benefits', 'Claims Expense', 'Loss and Loss Adjustment Expense' → Cost of Revenue for insurance companies.
AMORTIZATION OF DEFERRED CONTRACT COSTS: Goes to Cost of Revenue when it represents the cost of obtaining a customer contract.
negative_examples: Goodwill Impairment (Operating Expenses — write-down of acquired goodwill)
international_variants: Cost of Goods Sold (US GAAP standard)

Operating Expenses.description: Indirect operating costs incurred to support the business but NOT directly tied to producing individual units of product/service. These sit between Gross Profit and Operating Income (EBIT). Includes R&D, S&M, SG&A, D&A (on non-production assets), impairment charges, restructuring, and stock-based compensation when not allocated to other functions. The test: does this cost exist even if output were zero for a period? If yes → Operating Expenses.
disambiguation: EBIT / OPERATING INCOME: These are SUBTOTAL rows that result FROM operating expenses being deducted from gross profit. Classify as Operating Expenses since they're a computed subtotal within this section.

D&A PLACEMENT: Only classify here if the D&A label appears as a standalone line item in the income statement (often shown for transparency). Manufacturing companies embed D&A in Cost of Revenue; this line represents the non-production portion.
STOCK-BASED COMPENSATION: Often partially allocated across R&D, S&M, G&A. A standalone 'Stock-Based Compensation' line should be classified as Operating Expenses.
NON-INTEREST EXPENSE (BANKS): For banks, 'Non-Interest Expense' or 'Noninterest Expense' is the operating expense equivalent. Classify as Operating Expenses.
RESTRUCTURING: Always Operating Expenses, never Non-Operating. Under US GAAP and IFRS, restructuring charges are part of operating income/loss (eliminated from extraordinary classification in 2015).
GOODWILL IMPAIRMENT: Operating Expenses (a non-cash write-down within operating section).
TOTAL OPERATING EXPENSES: This is a SUBTOTAL row — include it as it belongs to the Operating Expenses section.
COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS, WAGES, SALARIES: Operating Expenses unless context makes it clear they are production workers (then Cost of Revenue). A generic label → Operating Expenses.
international_variants: Hanbai-hi Oyobi Ippan Kanri-hi / 販売費及び一般管理費 (Japanese SG&A)
Guanli Feiyong / 管理费用 (Chinese G&A)
Yanjiu Kaifa Feiyong / 研究开发费用 (Chinese R&D)

Non-Operating Items.description: Income and expenses BELOW operating income that arise from activities outside the company's core business operations. Primarily: interest on debt (financing cost), interest/dividend income (return on invested cash), FX gains/losses on monetary items, gains/losses from selling assets/investments, equity method income from associates, and other one-off incidental items. IFRS 18 (2024+) separates these into Investing and Financing sub-categories, but for classification purposes group all here.
disambiguation: INTEREST INCOME — NON-BANKS: Always Non-Operating (Investing category under IFRS 18). Exception: for banks and financial companies, interest income is core Revenue.
INTEREST EXPENSE — ALL NON-BANKS: Always Non-Operating (Financing category under IFRS 18). It is the cost of borrowed money, not core operations.
GAIN/LOSS ON SALE OF PP&E: Non-Operating. The proceeds go to Investing CF; the gain/loss appears here in IS. Never classify as Revenue.

EQUITY METHOD INCOME/LOSS: Non-Operating. Represents the company's share of an associate's profit/loss. Labels: 'Equity in Earnings of Associates', 'Share of Profit of Associates', 'Equity Method Income'.
TOTAL OTHER INCOME/EXPENSE (yfinance label): This is a rolled-up Non-Operating subtotal. Classify as Non-Operating Items.
TOTAL UNUSUAL ITEMS (yfinance): These are non-recurring, non-operating adjustments. Classify as Non-Operating Items.
GAIN ON SALE OF SECURITY (yfinance): This is a realized investment gain — Non-Operating Items.

PENSION NON-SERVICE COST: Under US GAAP (ASC 715), non-service pension costs (interest cost, expected return on plan assets) are Non-Operating. Service cost is Operating. Under IFRS 18: financing category.

FX GAIN/LOSS: Foreign currency transaction gains/losses on monetary items (receivables, payables, debt denominated in foreign currency) → Non-Operating. Translation gains/losses from consolidating foreign subsidiaries normally go to OCI (equity), not IS — if they appear in IS, they are Non-Operating.
SUBLEASE INCOME: Non-Operating for non-REIT companies (incidental activity). Revenue for REIT companies.
INSURANCE RECOVERY: Non-Operating (incidental receipt).
negative_examples: Net Interest Income for Banks (that is Revenue for banks)
Provision for Credit Losses for Banks (that is Cost of Revenue)
Revenue from subletting for REITs (that is Revenue for REITs)
Income Tax Expense (goes to Income Tax section)
international_variants: Financial Income / Financial Expense (IFRS common presentation)
Extraordinary Items (J-GAAP — items below ordinary income in Japanese companies)
Toku-betsu Rieki / 特別利益 (Japanese Extraordinary Gain)
Toku-betsu Sonshitsu / 特別損失 (Japanese Extraordinary Loss)
Ordinary Income (J-GAAP subtotal below operating profit including financial items)

Income Tax.description: All tax charges or benefits arising from the company's taxable income. Includes both current taxes (actually owed to tax authorities this year) and deferred taxes (future tax consequences of timing differences). This is always a separate line item below Pre-Tax Income.
disambiguation: DEFERRED INCOME TAX AS CASH FLOW ADJUSTMENT: In the Cash Flow Statement, 'Deferred Income Tax' or 'Deferred Tax Benefit' appears as an add-back to Net Income in Operating Activities. In the Income Statement, it appears as part of Income Tax Expense. Context determines classification.
TAX EFFECT OF UNUSUAL ITEMS (yfinance): This is an adjustment within income tax — classify as Income Tax.
TAX RATE FOR CALCS (yfinance): This is a ratio/metric field, not a line item. If present, classify as Income Tax.
WITHHOLDING TAX ON DIVIDENDS: Usually part of the company's income tax expense. Classify as Income Tax.
negative_examples: Deferred Tax Asset (Balance Sheet — Current or Non-Current Asset)
Deferred Tax Liability (Balance Sheet — Non-Current Liability)
international_variants: Suo De Shui Fei / 所得税费用 (Chinese)

Per Share Data.description: Per-share metrics and weighted-average share counts. These are not income/expense items but disclosures required at the bottom of the income statement. Includes basic and diluted EPS, share counts used to compute EPS, and dividends declared per share.
disambiguation: SHARES OUTSTANDING ON BALANCE SHEET vs EPS DENOMINATOR: Balance sheet shows period-end shares; EPS uses weighted-average. If the label is clearly related to EPS computation ('weighted average', 'diluted shares used'), classify as Per Share Data.
DILUTED EPS vs BASIC EPS: Both go here. Diluted includes dilutive securities (options, convertibles, warrants).
ADJUSTED/NON-GAAP EPS: Some companies report 'Adjusted EPS' or 'Non-GAAP EPS' — classify as Per Share Data.
negative_examples: Total Shares Outstanding (Balance Sheet equity section — Other Equity Items)
international_variants: Earnings Per Share Attributable to Owners (IFRS)
Basic and Diluted EPS from Continuing Operations (IFRS)
H株当たり当期純利益 (Japanese — EPS)
Mei Gu Shou Yi / 每股收益 (Chinese EPS)

Current Assets.description: Assets expected to be converted to cash, sold, or consumed within the company's normal operating cycle or 12 months, whichever is longer. Includes cash, near-cash, receivables, inventories, and prepayments. The defining question: will this asset be used or converted within one year or one operating cycle?
disambiguation: RESTRICTED CASH: If the restriction lifts within 12 months → Current Assets. If restricted for more than 12 months (e.g. collateral for a multi-year loan) → Non-Current Assets. If labeled without qualifier, use Current Assets as default.

CONTRACT ASSETS (ASC 606 / IFRS 15): Must be split current/non-current based on expected delivery timing. A label 'Contract Assets' without further qualifier → Current Assets (most performance obligations are short-cycle).

DEFERRED TAX ASSET (CURRENT): Under old US GAAP, deferred tax was split current/non-current. Under current US GAAP (ASC 740 update, 2015) all deferred tax is non-current. If labeled 'Deferred Tax Asset Current', use Current Assets for backward compatibility.
ASSETS HELD FOR SALE: Always Current Assets — IFRS 5 / ASC 360 require classification as current when actively being marketed for sale within 12 months.
CASH & ST INVESTMENTS (combined line): Common in yfinance/FMP aggregations — classify as Current Assets.
NOTES RECEIVABLE: Current if due within 12 months, non-current if longer. A generic 'Notes Receivable' defaults to Current Assets.
TOTAL CURRENT ASSETS: A subtotal row — include in Current Assets section.
negative_examples: Deferred Tax Asset (Non-Current Assets under current US GAAP)

Non-Current Assets.description: Assets expected to provide economic benefits beyond one year or one operating cycle. Includes long-term tangible assets (PP&E), intangibles (goodwill, patents), long-term investments, deferred taxes (under current standards), right-of-use assets, and other long-term assets. These are the 'productive backbone' of the business.
disambiguation: GOODWILL AND INTANGIBLES (combined): This is a common FMP/yfinance aggregation of goodwill + other intangibles — classify as Non-Current Assets.
TOTAL ASSETS: A grand subtotal — include in Non-Current Assets section (it is the terminal subtotal of assets).
DEFERRED TAX ASSETS: Under current US GAAP (post-2015 ASU 2015-17) ALL deferred tax is classified as non-current. Under older statements, may see current portion. Default → Non-Current Assets.
OPERATING LEASE RIGHT-OF-USE (ROU) ASSET: Always Non-Current under IFRS 16 and ASC 842 (with the CURRENT PORTION of the lease LIABILITY appearing in Current Liabilities separately).
EQUITY METHOD INVESTMENTS vs SHORT-TERM INVESTMENTS: Equity method (associates with significant influence, typically 20-50% stake) → Non-Current. Short-term marketable securities → Current.
LONG-TERM RESTRICTED CASH: If cash is pledged as collateral for a loan with >12 months remaining, or is legally restricted for >12 months → Non-Current.
CONTENT ASSETS / FILM COSTS (Netflix/Disney): Capitalized content production costs — Non-Current intangibles.
EXPLORATION ASSETS (Mining): Capitalized exploration and evaluation costs — Non-Current Assets.
international_variants: Fei Liudong Zichan / 非流动资产 (Chinese)

Current Liabilities.description: Obligations the company must settle within one year or one operating cycle, whichever is longer. Includes trade payables, short-term borrowings, the current portion of long-term debt, accrued expenses, deferred revenue expected to be earned within 12 months, and lease liabilities due within 12 months.
disambiguation: SHORT-TERM DEBT vs CURRENT PORTION OF LONG-TERM DEBT: Both are Current Liabilities. ST Debt is revolving/commercial paper; Current Portion is the installment of LTD due this year. Both common in yfinance/FMP — classify both as Current Liabilities.
DEFERRED REVENUE CURRENT: Revenue collected in advance, service to be delivered within 12 months → Current Liabilities. Multi-year contracts → split, with >12 months portion in Non-Current.
CONTRACT LIABILITIES (ASC 606): Same concept as deferred revenue. Current portion → Current Liabilities.
OPERATING LEASE LIABILITY CURRENT: The amount of the ROU lease obligation due within 12 months → Current Liabilities. (The non-current portion → Non-Current Liabilities.)
TOTAL CURRENT LIABILITIES: A subtotal row — include in Current Liabilities section.
negative_examples: Deferred Tax Liabilities (Non-Current Liabilities under current standards)

Non-Current Liabilities.description: Obligations due beyond one year or one operating cycle. The 'long-term financing' side of the balance sheet. Includes long-term debt, long-term lease liabilities, deferred tax liabilities, pension obligations, asset retirement obligations, and deferred revenue for multi-year contracts.
disambiguation: TOTAL LIABILITIES: A grand subtotal row — include in Non-Current Liabilities section (terminal subtotal of liabilities).
TOTAL NON-CURRENT LIABILITIES: Subtotal row — include here.
DEFERRED TAX LIABILITIES: Under current US GAAP (post-2015) ALL deferred tax liabilities are non-current. Classify here.

LONG-TERM DEBT TOTAL: Some providers show 'Total Debt' which combines short + long-term debt. If labeled 'Total Debt' without qualifier and it's a balance sheet item, classify as Non-Current (the majority is typically long-term). Alternatively this may be a computed metric — context dependent.
OPERATING LEASE LONG-TERM PORTION: The multi-year portion of ROU lease obligations → Non-Current Liabilities.
PENSION: Always Non-Current regardless of amount expected to be paid in next year (the current portion of pension payments is typically small and often grouped with the long-term obligation).
negative_examples: Current Portion of Long-Term Debt (Current Liabilities)
international_variants: Fei Liudong Fuzhai / 非流动负债 (Chinese)

Contributed Capital.description: Capital injected by shareholders through the issuance of stock. Represents the amount shareholders paid to the company for their ownership stake. Includes the par value of shares issued AND the premium paid above par (APIC). This is NOT retained earnings (past profits) — it is what shareholders actively paid in.
examples: Capital in Excess of Par Value
disambiguation: PREFERRED STOCK vs REDEEMABLE PREFERRED: Standard preferred stock with no mandatory redemption → Contributed Capital. Mandatorily redeemable preferred stock (which must be paid back like debt) → it is mezzanine equity or a liability, not pure equity. A generic 'Preferred Stock' label → Contributed Capital.
SHARE PREMIUM (IFRS/UK): This is the APIC equivalent — the amount received above par value — classify as Contributed Capital.
COMMON STOCK PAR VALUE: Very small amount (e.g. $0.001 per share × shares) — still Contributed Capital.
STOCK OPTIONS/WARRANTS OUTSTANDING: If shown as an equity component → Contributed Capital.
negative_examples: Treasury Stock (Other Equity Items — it reduces equity)
international_variants: Ziben Gong Ji / 资本公积 (Chinese APIC)
Gu Ben / 股本 (Chinese share capital)

Earned Capital.description: Accumulated profits generated by the company and retained in the business rather than distributed as dividends. This is the cumulative total of all Net Income since inception, minus all dividends declared. A deficit (negative retained earnings) means the company has accumulated losses. This is the 'internally generated' equity.
disambiguation: ACCUMULATED DEFICIT: A negative retained earnings balance (common for growth companies and startups). Still classify as Earned Capital — same account, just negative.

RESERVES (IFRS/HKFRS): Under IFRS, 'Other Reserves' or 'Statutory Reserves' may appear alongside retained earnings as a separate component — these reflect regulatory requirements to retain a portion of profits. Classify as Earned Capital.
REVALUATION SURPLUS (IFRS): Gains from revaluing PP&E at fair value — technically part of OCI and shown in Other Comprehensive Income → classify as Other Equity Items (not Earned Capital).
international_variants: Wei Fen Pei Li Run / 未分配利润 (Chinese)

Other Equity Items.description: Equity components that are neither contributed capital nor retained earnings. Includes: (1) Treasury Stock — the cost of repurchased shares which reduces equity; (2) Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income (AOCI/OCI) — unrealized gains/losses on hedges, pension adjustments, currency translation; (3) Non-Controlling Interests (NCI/Minority Interests) — the portion of consolidated subsidiaries not owned by the parent; (4) Other reserves.
disambiguation: TREASURY STOCK: A contra-equity item (reduces total equity). It represents the cost of shares bought back from the market. Negative balance is normal. Classify as Other Equity Items.

AOCI vs RETAINED EARNINGS: Unrealized gains/losses on AFS securities, cash flow hedges, pension adjustments, and foreign currency translation all go to AOCI (Other Equity Items), NOT retained earnings. They bypass the income statement.
MINORITY INTEREST / NON-CONTROLLING INTEREST: Under IFRS and US GAAP, NCI is presented within total equity (not as a liability). Classify as Other Equity Items.
TOTAL STOCKHOLDERS EQUITY / TOTAL EQUITY: Grand subtotal row — include in Other Equity Items section (terminal subtotal of equity).
REVALUATION SURPLUS (IFRS option for PP&E): When a company elects the revaluation model for PP&E, the upward revaluation goes to OCI/Other Equity Items.
SUBSCRIPTION RECEIVABLE: An amount still owed by shareholders on partly-paid shares — it is a contra-equity item similar to treasury stock. Other Equity Items.
negative_examples: Retained Earnings (Earned Capital — that is accumulated profits)
international_variants: Non-Controlling Interests (IFRS standard label since IFRS 3 2008)
Minority Interest (older IFRS / US GAAP pre-2009)
Capital and Reserves Attributable to Non-Controlling Interests
Other Reserves (IFRS — statutory, capital redemption, hedging reserves)
Qi Ta Zong He Shou Yi / 其他综合收益 (Chinese OCI)
Shazoku-Kabunushi-Mochibun / 少数株主持分 (Japanese Minority Interest)

Operating Activities.description: Cash generated or consumed by the company's core day-to-day operations. Under the INDIRECT METHOD (most common), starts with Net Income and adjusts for: (1) non-cash charges added back (D&A, SBC, impairments, deferred taxes), (2) gains/losses removed (asset sale gains subtracted because proceeds are in Investing), and (3) working capital changes (receivables, inventories, payables, accruals). The result is the actual cash the business generated from running its operations.
examples: Changes in Contract Assets and Liabilities
disambiguation: NET INCOME IN CF STATEMENT: 'Net Income' as the STARTING LINE of the Cash Flow statement (indirect method) belongs here in Operating Activities. This is the same number as the IS bottom line — used as the reconciliation starting point.

GAIN ON SALE OF ASSETS (CF adjustment): When a gain appears in Operating Activities CF, it is being SUBTRACTED (the actual proceeds are in Investing Activities, so the gain is removed from operations). If labeled as an adjustment within CFO → Operating Activities.
LOSS ON DISPOSAL: Added back in Operating Activities as a non-cash / reclassification adjustment.

DEFERRED INCOME TAX: In the CF statement, this is an Operating adjustment (non-cash add-back). In the IS, it is a component of Income Tax Expense. Context determines placement — in CF context → Operating Activities.
PENSION EXPENSE: Only the non-cash service cost portion appears in Operating Activities. Actual cash contributions may also appear here.
CHANGES IN WORKING CAPITAL (AGGREGATE): Often a single line 'Change in Working Capital' — Operating Activities.
AMORTIZATION OF DEFERRED FINANCING COSTS: Non-cash interest-related amortization → typically shown within Operating Activities as a non-cash add-back.
negative_examples: Capital Expenditures (Investing Activities — cash spent on PP&E)

Investing Activities.description: Cash spent or received from acquiring and disposing of LONG-TERM ASSETS and INVESTMENTS. This is how the company deploys capital to grow or maintain its productive base. Outflows: CapEx (buying PP&E), acquisitions of businesses, purchases of investments. Inflows: proceeds from selling assets, divesting businesses, maturing investments. High negative investing CF is often a sign of a growing company investing in its future.
keywords: purchases of property plant and equipment
proceeds from sale of marketable securities
sales of property plant and equipment
examples: Purchases of Property, Plant and Equipment
Net Cash Used in Investing Activities
disambiguation: CAPITAL EXPENDITURES (CapEx): The single most important Investing Activities line item. Always here. Labeled as 'Capital Expenditures', 'Capex', 'Purchase of PP&E', 'Additions to Fixed Assets', etc.
ACQUISITIONS: Cash paid to acquire another company (net of cash acquired) → Investing Activities.

PURCHASES OF MARKETABLE SECURITIES vs SHORT-TERM INVESTMENTS: If these are described as 'purchases of investments' or 'purchases of marketable securities' in the CF statement → Investing Activities. (Short-term investments as a BALANCE SHEET item → Current Assets.)
CAPITALIZED SOFTWARE / CONTENT: Cash spent to develop software or create content that is capitalized (not expensed) → Investing Activities (similar to CapEx).
PROCEEDS FROM ASSET SALES: The CASH received from selling PP&E or investments → Investing Activities. The GAIN/LOSS from the sale is in the IS (Non-Operating) and CF as an operating adjustment.
LOANS ORIGINATED (for financial companies): Banks originating loans to customers → Investing Activities (asset creation).
negative_examples: Gain on Sale of Assets as P&L line (Non-Operating Items in IS)

Free Cash Flow.description: A non-GAAP/non-IFRS metric computed as Operating Cash Flow minus Capital Expenditures. Represents the cash the business generates after maintaining and growing its asset base — the cash available to repay debt, pay dividends, or buy back shares. Some data providers (FMP, yfinance) calculate and present this directly as a line item in the CF statement.
disambiguation: FREE CASH FLOW IS A DERIVED METRIC: It equals 'Cash Flow from Operations' minus 'Capital Expenditures'. It does not appear in statutory financial statements but is computed and presented by data providers (FMP, yfinance) as a convenience row.
LEVERED FCF (FCFE): After debt service — cash available to equity holders. Still classify as Free Cash Flow.
UNLEVERED FCF (FCFF): Before debt service — used in DCF valuation. Still classify as Free Cash Flow.
FFO (REIT): Funds From Operations is NOT the same as FCF but serves an analogous role for REITs. If labeled 'FFO', classify as Free Cash Flow.
negative_examples: Operating Cash Flow (Operating Activities — the starting point for FCF calculation)
Capital Expenditures (Investing Activities — the deduction in FCF calculation)

Financing Activities.description: Cash flows between the company and its capital providers — debt holders and equity holders. How the company raises money (debt issuance, equity issuance) and returns it (debt repayment, dividends, buybacks). Lease payments under IFRS 16 / ASC 842 also appear here. High negative financing CF can indicate debt repayment and/or shareholder returns — a sign of maturity.
keywords: proceeds from exercise of stock options
examples: Proceeds from Issuance of Common Stock
Proceeds from Exercise of Stock Options
disambiguation: DIVIDENDS PAID: Always Financing Activities (return of capital to equity holders). Note: Under IFRS, dividends paid CAN be classified as Operating Activities, but most companies classify as Financing.
SHARE BUYBACKS / REPURCHASES: Financing Activities — the company is returning cash to equity holders.
PROCEEDS FROM STOCK OPTION EXERCISES: Financing Activities — company receives cash from employee stock option exercises.
TAXES PAID ON RSU VESTING (shares withheld): Financing Activities — equivalent to buying back shares to cover employee tax withholding.

LEASE PAYMENTS (IFRS 16 / ASC 842): Principal portions of both operating lease AND finance lease payments → Financing Activities. The interest portion of finance leases → may be Operating or Financing per policy choice.
PROCEEDS FROM DEBT vs PROCEEDS FROM INVESTMENTS: Debt proceeds (loans, bonds) → Financing. Proceeds from selling investment securities → Investing.
ENDING CASH / NET CHANGE IN CASH: These are summary/reconciling rows at the end of the CF statement — classify as Financing Activities (they belong to the bottom of the statement).

CONTINGENT CONSIDERATION PAYMENTS: If paid after the acquisition date → Financing (up to original fair value at acquisition) or Operating (any excess over original fair value). A generic label → Financing Activities.
DIVIDENDS RECEIVED: Under US GAAP → Operating Activities. Under IFRS → Operating or Investing (policy choice). Distinguish from 'Dividends Paid' which is always Financing.
